correctness.rationale: For KG(n,2), n>=6, disjoint vertex-label pairs have metric distance 1 and intersecting pairs have distance 2. Every L1 cut semimetric has conditional negative type on zero-sum vectors: sum(z_e z_f rho(e,f))=-2(sum_(e in S)z_e)^2<=0. Symmetrization over S_n reduces rho to values u (disjoint) and v (intersecting). With unsigned incidence matrix B and A=B^TB−2I, vector z=B^Ta (sum a=0) lies in the eigenvalue (n−4) subspace, forcing (n−4)v<=(n−3)u, so D>=2(n−4)/(n−3). For the Hamilton-cycle edge-set cut orbit, elementary disjoint/intersecting crossing fractions p_D=4(n−4)/((n−1)(n−2)), p_I=4(n−3)/((n−1)(n−2)). Scaling the averaged nonnegative cut metric by 2/p_I gives intersecting distance 2 and disjoint distance D, proving the upper bound. Independent exact intersection/crossing tests on 46449 unordered vertex-label pairs over n=6..18; finite checks not all-n proof.
